correctness.rationale: All hypotheses, normalizations and invariant boundaries are specified. Exact log-product identity is verified algebraically. Positivity, uniform boundedness, positive lower logistic comparison and monotone product prove global interior attraction. Exact slaving quotient equations converge by variation of constants and yield the cubic and quartic reduced coefficients; reciprocal-square integration establishes the two-term law with initial-condition-independent constants. Standalone standard-library checker reproduced 1968 exact rational identities/coefficient checks and six finite numerical sanity checks. The proof, not simulations, supports infinite-time quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison with Xia et al. arXiv:2310.10558v1 distinguishes the already published local cubic normal form and equilibrium classification from the new global equality-case monotone product, basin-wide extinction and universal quartic/second coefficient. Published analogous critical models examined in full concern different equations; published-finding corpus and accessible own-record searches found no dominating statement. This is best-knowledge priority, not a uniqueness certificate. An additional full-text 2023 two-patch comparison (Grumbach et al.) uses linear transport and focuses on stationary total population size, so does not dominate the extinction-rate claim.
residual_risks: A broad nonlinear-center-manifold result or unindexed prior model-specific derivation could imply the exact higher-order coefficient and reduce the originality scope.
The 2023 initiating paper already supplies a nonzero local cubic coefficient; neither the leading exponent alone nor its equilibrium classification is asserted new.

Full text was inspected for the identical-model primary and the two closest published records; full text of the 2024 discrete companion and 2017 general article was not inspected, so no full-text negative priority finding is made for those articles.

value.rationale: A precisely motivated ecological threshold determines whether loss of the Allee-affected patch is inverse-time or inverse-square-root; the equality case exhibits a universal, nontrivial second coefficient that measures nonlinear dispersal. The globally decreasing product supplies a structural proof for all interior initial data, not a finite-census artifact or textbook parameter substitution. Applicable to critical relaxation/finite-window observations within the normalized continuous-time model.
